misconceptions.description: Believing that recorded videos plus end-of-module quizzes constitute a complete online course
misconceptions.trigger: learner equates 'has videos and quizzes' with 'has all needed interactions'
misconceptions.feedback: Videos and auto-graded quizzes only support learner-content interaction. Defensible online design also includes deliberate learner-instructor and learner-learner interaction.

misconceptions.description: Treating exploratory forum discussion as evidence of deep learning
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites high post counts as proof of cognitive presence
misconceptions.feedback: Cognitive presence requires moving past exploration into integration and resolution. High-volume forums that never synthesize are stalled at the exploration phase.

misconceptions.description: Using synchronous time to deliver one-way lectures that could be asynchronous
misconceptions.trigger: learner schedules webinars as 90-minute one-way broadcasts
misconceptions.feedback: Synchronous time is most valuable for real-time discourse and immediate feedback. One-way content delivery should almost always be asynchronous so learners can pace and rewatch.

misconceptions.description: Equating teaching presence with on-camera instructor visibility
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues that any course where the instructor appears on camera has strong teaching presence
misconceptions.feedback: Teaching presence is the design and direction of the experience — architecture, facilitation, direct instruction. Camera time is one expression, not the construct itself.
